summary: Big Ten coaches are angry that the conference and commissioner Tony Petitti have taken no action over Michigan's alleged sign-stealing scheme, according to coaches who spoke to The Athletic after a Wednesday video call. They argue the scheme gave Michigan a major advantage and call it "damn near espionage." The NCAA investigation is ongoing and slow, the Big Ten lacks its own investigators, and sources at four schools don't expect punishment before the season ends.
one_line: Big Ten coaches voice anger at commissioner Tony Petitti's inaction over Michigan's alleged sign-stealing scheme, calling it "damn near espionage," while the NCAA investigation drags on.
key_facts: Big Ten coaches voiced frustration on a Wednesday video call with commissioner Tony Petitti after Jim Harbaugh left the call; they don't feel Petitti is "motivated" to act against Michigan.

One Big Ten coach said Harbaugh is under investigation for three things: alleged illegal signal stealing, alleged illegal recruiting during COVID, and an investigation into the offensive coordinator and alleged computer hacking.
One coach said, "This was damn near espionage," and argued the scheme forces teams to teach players a whole new way to communicate.
A third Big Ten head coach said Michigan had been cheating the game for two-and-a-half years and "might as well have been playing with 15 guys on the field."
The NCAA is investigating Michigan's football program over allegations of illegal in-person scouting and recording of signals.
Ahead of the Oct. 21 Michigan-Michigan State game, the Big Ten told MSU it was aware of "credible evidence" of sign-stealing and said it would monitor the NCAA investigation.

The Big Ten can act under its sportsmanship policy but has no investigators of its own and relies on the NCAA; it's unclear what punishment coaches want, since banning Michigan from the Big Ten championship would harm uninvolved players.
Sources at four different Big Ten schools said they don't expect the conference to punish Michigan before the season ends.
Michigan suspended staffer Connor Stalions with pay on Oct. 20; he is at the center of the NCAA investigation.

Stalions bought tickets to games in at least seven Big Ten stadiums before those teams played Michigan over the past three seasons; buying tickets isn't a violation, but using them to scout and record is.
Central Michigan is investigating whether Stalions was on its sideline at the Sept. 1 game at Michigan State, after photos circulated online.
Purdue coach Ryan Walters said "They aren't allegations. It happened," citing video evidence and trackable ticket purchases, and said his team had to learn a new language.
Harbaugh has denied knowledge of the alleged scouting.
